hypothesis: Completion takes its cart lock and reservation lock through the default in-memory locking provider, which only serializes requests inside one Medusa process. With two servers sharing one database, two simultaneous complete calls on the same cart can each pass the order_cart existence check and each create an order, so one cart ends up linked to two orders (one_order_per_cart fails). A second expected effect is oversell on the single-unit SOLO item if both servers reserve it at once.
submitted_scenario:
schema: oversold.scenario/v1
name: cart-double-complete-two-servers
description: One cart is completed simultaneously on two servers, each server holding its own process-local lock.
target:
  engine: medusa
  version: 2.22.0
  servers: 2
stock:
  SOLO: 1
carts:
  alice:
    server: 1
    count: 1
    lines:
    - sku: OVS-SOLO
      qty: 1
race:
- id: complete-on-server-1
  server: 1
  do: complete
  cart: alice
- id: complete-on-server-2
  server: 2
  do: complete
  cart: alice
timing:
  release: together
  jitter_ms:
  - 0
  - 3
faults: []
runs: 20
seed: 7

hypothesis: Two different carts each hold the single SOLO unit and are completed at the same moment on two servers. The reservation lock is process-local, so both servers can read stocked=1 with no reservation and both reserve it, giving an oversell (no_oversell and reserved_matches_reservations are the likely failures).
